proto.description: How the interface is addressed: dhcp to ask a DHCP server, or manual to bring it up with no address.

external.description: Marks a device phenix does not deploy, such as hardware in the loop. It stays in the topology for State of Health and apps.

hostname.description: Name of the device in the topology.

notes.description: Notes about the device. phenix copies them to the device's labels, as notes, when an experiment is created.
example: Physical PLC on the test bench.

vm_type.description: Whether the device is a virtual machine or a container.

memory.description: Memory of the device, in megabytes.

vcpus.description: Number of CPUs of the device.

interfaces.description: Network interfaces of the device, for the topology's network diagram and State of Health checks.

mask.description: Network prefix length (CIDR bits), from 0 to 32.

proto.description: How the interface gets its address: static, dhcp, or manual for none.

type.description: What the device is, such as HIL for hardware in the loop.

autostart.description: Whether the interface should come up when the VM boots. phenix itself does not act on this setting.

bridge.description: Open vSwitch bridge on the host the interface attaches to. Empty or phenix uses the experiment's default bridge.

driver.description: Emulated network card, such as e1000 or virtio-net-pci. Empty uses minimega's default.

mac.description: MAC address. minimega generates one when it is empty.

mtu.description: Maximum transmission unit, in bytes. Vyatta and VyOS routers apply values from 68 to 16000; other images keep their own.

name.description: Interface name, such as eth0, which NAT settings and apps use to refer to it.

qinq.description: Carry the guest's own VLAN tags inside the interface's VLAN (QinQ, 802.1ad). The guest brings the interface up without an address.

anyOf.description: DNS server addresses the guest uses: one address, or a list.

gateway.description: Default gateway, reached through this interface.

mask.description: Network prefix length (CIDR bits), from 0 to 32.

ruleset_in.description: Ruleset for traffic coming in on this interface, on Router and Firewall nodes.

ruleset_out.description: Ruleset for traffic going out of this interface, on Router and Firewall nodes.

advanced.description: Extra minimega vm config settings, each a setting name and its value.

commands.description: minimega command and control (cc) commands phenix sends to the VM, such as exec df -h.

c2.description: Start the VM once each of these hosts has checked in with minimega command and control.

useUUID.description: Wait for the host's UUID, rather than its hostname, to check in.

timer.description: Start the VM this long after the experiment starts, as a duration such as 30s or 5m.

user.description: Leave the VM stopped until someone starts it from phenix or minimega. Takes precedence over the other delays.

do_not_boot.description: Leave the node out when the experiment starts: phenix neither creates nor starts its VM. phenix also sets this when the first drive's image is missing.

hostname.description: Name of the VM in minimega and the host name set in the guest. Unique in the topology.

notes.description: Notes about the node. phenix copies them to the VM's notes when an experiment is created.
example: Domain controller for the corporate network.
Reset the administrator password before each run.

snapshot.description: Run the VM on a copy-on-write snapshot of its first drive, which phenix creates for the experiment and injects files into, so the image file itself does not change. phenix turns this on when it is not set.

vm_type.description: How minimega runs the node: kvm for a QEMU/KVM virtual machine, or container. Empty means kvm.

cpu.description: QEMU CPU model for the VM, such as Broadwell or host.

drives.description: Disks attached to the VM, in order. The first is the one phenix snapshots and injects files into.

cache_mode.description: QEMU cache mode for the disk. Empty uses writeback for a snapshot, and QEMU's default otherwise.

image.description: Disk image file: a name in the phenix image directory, or an absolute path on the host.

inject_partition.description: Partition of the first drive that phenix injects files into. 0 skips disk injection, and phenix sends its startup scripts through minimega command and control instead. phenix uses 1 when it is not set.

interface.description: Bus the disk is attached to, such as ide, scsi or virtio. Empty uses minimega's default.

memory.description: Memory for the VM, in megabytes. phenix uses 512 when it is not set.

os_type.description: Operating system in the disk image. phenix and its apps choose startup scripts and router configuration by it.

vcpus.description: Number of virtual CPUs. phenix uses 1 when it is not set.

injections.description: Files phenix copies into the snapshot of the first drive before the VM starts.

dst.description: Path the file is written to in the guest.

permissions.description: File mode for the copied file, in octal such as 0664.

src.description: File on the phenix host: an absolute path, or a path relative to the experiment directory.

interfaces.description: Network interfaces, in the order the guest sees them.

areas.description: OSPF areas the router takes part in.

area_id.description: OSPF area number. 0 is the backbone area.

area_networks.description: Networks the router advertises in the area.

network.description: Network in CIDR notation, such as 10.1.25.0/24.

dead_interval.description: Seconds without a hello from a neighbor before the router considers it down. Applies to interfaces whose protocol is ospf.

hello_interval.description: Seconds between OSPF hello packets. Applies to interfaces whose protocol is ospf.

retransmission_interval.description: Seconds before the router resends a link-state advertisement that was not acknowledged. Applies to interfaces whose protocol is ospf.

router_id.description: OSPF router ID, written like an IPv4 address, such as 0.0.0.1.

routes.description: Static routes phenix configures in the guest.

cost.description: Route cost, set as the administrative distance on Vyatta and VyOS routers.

destination.description: Network to reach, in CIDR notation such as 192.168.0.0/24.

next.description: Address of the next hop toward the destination.

rulesets.description: Firewall rulesets for Router and Firewall nodes. An interface applies one by naming it as its inbound or outbound ruleset.

default.description: What happens to traffic that no rule matches.

description.description: Describes the ruleset in the router configuration.
description.example: From Corp to the DMZ network

name.description: Name interfaces use to apply the ruleset.

action.description: What happens to traffic the rule matches.

description.description: Describes the rule in the router configuration.

address.description: Destination address or network the rule matches.

port.description: Destination port the rule matches. Empty or 0 matches any port.

id.description: Rule number, unique in the ruleset. Vyatta and VyOS routers check rules from the lowest number up.

protocol.description: Protocol of the traffic the rule matches.

address.description: Source address or network the rule matches.

port.description: Source port the rule matches. Empty or 0 matches any port.

type.description: What the node is. phenix configures Router and Firewall nodes whose OS type is vyatta, vyos or minirouter as routers, from their interfaces, routes, OSPF settings and rulesets.

baud_rate.description: Speed of the serial line, in bits per second.

device.description: Serial device the guest uses, such as /dev/ttyS0.

proto.description: Serial interfaces have a static address.

type.description: Kind of interface: a serial link, carried over the network between VMs.

udp_port.description: UDP port that carries the serial traffic between VMs.

proto.description: How the interface is addressed: static for a fixed address, or ospf for a fixed address that also takes part in OSPF on a router.
